story: Scala: A software tool for microtonic, macrotonic and other alternative tunings
text: The list of export formats is really impressive. It's interesting to note that Hauptwerk (a pipe organ software emulator) is among the supported targets; some early organs used historical temperaments which sound different compared to equal temperament and some of those had split keys [1][2]. [1] This is an example of meantone organ with split sharps [VIDEO] [2] This is an explanation of Meantone and split keys [LINK]

story: Why are D-sharp and E-flat considered to be two different notes?
text: No, and yes. The difference is obvious even those who don't distinguish pitches much (can you hear the difference in the video linked in the article - [VIDEO] ) because the 'wrong' one played in a scale or a chord sounds really, really horrible; that's why we have all the work done on 'tempered' tuning to reduce the gap so that everything is just slightly off.
